interpretation: On the V14 synthetic fixture, compiling is latency-beneficial only after enough repeated reads amortize generation build cost. A workload with high semantic churn or low reuse can rationally stay on online indexed/SQL/graph lookup even when compiled hot reads are much faster.
architecture_consequence: Adaptive read routing must estimate reuse horizon and invalidation/churn before choosing COMPILED_INTENT_FIELD. Compilation is a workload decision, not an epistemic preference.
limitations: Derived from synthetic local-tool-container timing, not Hostinger or Andreas target hardware.
Ignores memory, I/O, concurrency, energy and rebuild contention unless already reflected in measured build/read latency.
Break-even changes with generation size, batch build strategy, query distribution and hardware.
Does not compare PostgreSQL/pgvector, a dedicated graph engine or late-interaction retrieval.
